text: There are 3 stamps on the counters in this kitchen. Stamp the final board so it shows exactly the pattern on the reference card, then press Submit. The final board is the blue-bordered one with the printed 3x3 grid; the green-bordered reference card is not for stamping. The round self-inking stamps stand face down on the work surface. Each prints a fixed pattern of dots in whatever direction it is held, and the unmarked housings show neither the pattern nor which way it points, so try them on the tan scratch board. Ink stays where it lands, on the scratch board and on the final board alike. Fill exactly the reference card's grid cells with no ink outside the final board's grid, put every stamp back down on the counter and let go, then press the red SUBMIT button. Your first submission ends the episode; a wrong submission or no submission fails. Other objects on the counter are not part of the task; you may move them if needed. You act through helper actions; the helpers move objects exactly. Instead of pressing Submit, give your answer with SUBMIT.
intro: On the work surface stamps 1 to 2 stand face down, numbered from left to right as the left camera sees them: stamp 1 (brown handle), stamp 2 (blue handle). The round stamp housings are unmarked. The green reference card shows the target pattern .X./.XX/..X (far row first, each row from left to right as the robot sees it; X is a dot, . is blank). The blue final board shows an empty 3x3 grid. The tan scratch board is blank. It has room for four prints that do not overlap: slot 1 back left, slot 2 back right, slot 3 front left, slot 4 front right (as the robot sees it).
help:
PRINT a IN SLOT s TURN r - press stamp a on the scratch board in slot s (1 back left, 2 back right, 3 front left, 4 front right), turned r quarter turns counterclockwise seen from above (r = 0 to 3) from the way it stands, and put it back where it stood. The print turns with the stamp. Ink is permanent: a used slot keeps its dots and adds the new ones
LOOK AROUND THE KITCHEN - look for stamps in the other parts of the kitchen
SUBMIT a:r b:r ... - your answer: press each named stamp a, turned r quarter turns as in PRINT, centred on the final board, and put every stamp back down (e.g. SUBMIT 1:0 3:2). Patterns read (far row first, each row from left to right as the robot sees it; X is a dot, . is blank)
